clue.text: 'Want to hide' made literal?

definitions.note: in printing, a literal is a typing slip, so a word made literal has been spelt wrongly

parts.note: to want for something is to miss it
a pelt is an animal's hide

explanation.surface: A puzzling instruction to take the phrase 'want to hide' at face value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made literal' looks like 'taken at face value', but a literal is the printer's word for a typo.
explanation.definitionFit: A word turned into a printer's literal has been written with a slip in its letters.

clue.text: Some numbers — but only some — that can appear on computer screen

definitions.text: that can appear on computer screen

indicators.note: but only some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Only some numbers can appear on a computer screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A menu is a list of options displayed on a computer screen.

clue.text: Extra payment required by cleaner having to sweep around

indicators.note: around says the word for sweep goes round the other piece

parts.note: a surge is a rushing sweep forward, as of water
a char is a British word for a cleaning lady

explanation.surface: A cleaner charges extra for sweeping round the place.
explanation.definitionFit: A surcharge is an additional fee added on top of the normal price.

clue.text: An old king playing harp with two exam levels (hard)

indicators.note: playing says the letters of harp are performed in a new order

parts.note: A and O levels are British school exams
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: An ancient king plays the harp while taking two exams.
explanation.walkthrough: A-levels and O-levels are British school exam grades.
explanation.definitionFit: Pharaoh was the title of the rulers of ancient Egypt.

clue.text: City with its tax body sets forms etc

definitions.note: a set is a badger's home and a form is a hare's, both animal dens

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
the IRS is the Internal Revenue Service, the US tax authority

explanation.surface: A city's tax office sends out forms and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sets' and 'forms' look like paperwork but are animals' homes.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is a wild animal's den, of which a badger's set and a hare's form are examples.

clue.text: Rum and whiskey, dire when mixed

parts.note: W is Whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: when mixed says the letters of the pieces before it are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A drinker finds a cocktail of rum and whiskey dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' poses as the drink; it is the old adjective for odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum is an old British adjective for strange or odd, a synonym.

clue.text: Out of control it clawed scratching everyone finally?

definitions.text: Out of control it clawed scratching everyone finally?

indicators.note: out of control says the letters of it clawed are thrown into disorder
scratching means striking out, so a letter is cancelled from the mix
finally picks out the closing letter of everyone

explanation.surface: A wild animal ran amok and clawed at everyone in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffle IT CLAWED less E (the last of 'everyone'); the whole clue also describes the beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A wildcat is a fierce feline that, out of control, would claw people.

clue.text: Independent makes study of revered art

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study closely

explanation.surface: The Independent newspaper runs a study of revered works of art.
explanation.definitionFit: Icons are sacred images venerated in Orthodox churches, so pieces of revered art.

clue.text: "A Princess's Prince" — a newspaper editor's mocked

parts.note: Di is the familiar name of Diana, Princess of Wales, so a princess's is Di's
a rag is slang for a low-grade newspaper

explanation.surface: A tabloid editor mocks a headline about a princess's prince.
explanation.definitionFit: To disparage is to belittle or scorn, so disparaged means treated with mockery.

clue.text: Maybe he incenses by means of someone ranting?

definitions.note: incense here means to scent with incense, which a maker of scents might do

parts.note: per means by means of, as in per post
one who fumes rages, so a fumer is someone ranting

explanation.surface: A ranting person infuriates others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incenses' reads as angers, but here means fills with fragrant smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: A maker of fragrances could be said to scent things, the other sense of incense.

clue.text: Account of arrival in Natal

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: natal, meaning of one's birth, is a synonym of native
ARR is the timetable abbreviation for arrival

explanation.surface: A report describing someone's arrival in the South African province of Natal.
explanation.walkthrough: Natal looks like the place name; it is the adjective meaning of birth, as in native land.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative is a story or account of events, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Twists bobbin around

indicators.note: around says the word for the bobbin is turned back to front

parts.note: a bobbin is a spool for thread

explanation.surface: Thread wound round a bobbin gets twisted.
explanation.definitionFit: Loops are twists or turns in a line or thread, a synonym as plural nouns.

clue.text: Mark's hip replacement in vessels at sea (clippers)

indicators.note: replacement in says one stretch of the vessels' word is swapped out for another

parts.note: vessels at sea are ships
taken as written: the letters of hip inside the word for vessels
to mark someone's words is to hear them

explanation.surface: Mark's hip joint is replaced while he is aboard ship, with clippers in brackets.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the HIP in SHIPS for HEAR ('mark', as in mark my words).
explanation.definitionFit: Shears are large scissors, a cutting tool also called clippers.

clue.text: Fantastic if such is planted next to a flowering shrub

indicators.note: planted next to says one piece is set down beside the other in the answer
fantastic means wild and fanciful, so the letters of if such are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something fantastic, if such a thing is planted beside a flowering shrub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fantastic' rearranges IF SUCH into FUCHSI; 'planted next to' then sets A after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The fuchsia is a garden shrub grown for its drooping pink and purple flowers.

clue.text: See addict gets sorted with a small black suit that's sterile

indicators.note: gets sorted says the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: C is a small letter for clubs, a black suit in cards

explanation.surface: An addict gets sorted out with a small black suit that looks sterile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets sorted' rearranges SEE ADDICT plus C (clubs).
explanation.definitionFit: Desiccated means dried out, and figuratively dull and lifeless, so sterile.

clue.text: Annoying jingle about Telford's top hotel and 'The Early Bird's Breakfast'?

indicators.note: about says the jingle's word goes round the other letters

parts.note: an earworm is a catchy tune that sticks in the head

indicators.note: top picks out the opening letter of Telford

parts.note: H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A jingle advertising a Telford hotel's breakfast, called The Early Bird's Breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the proverb that the early bird catches the worm. Telford is a town in Shropshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial early bird catches a worm, so the creature it eats is jokingly its breakfast.

clue.text: Go beyond six ball throws and maybe dog's upset

parts.note: in cricket an over is six balls bowled

indicators.note: upset says the word is turned upside down, reading upwards in this down entry

parts.note: a dog is an example of a pet, so dog's is pet's

explanation.surface: A dog is upset by six balls thrown in a row.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: To overstep is to go past a limit, exceeding what is allowed.

clue.text: A letter and article you shouldn't have

parts.note: the is the definite article
said on receiving a gift, a way of saying thanks, which in British slang is ta

explanation.surface: A letter and a newspaper article that the reader should never have been sent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You shouldn't have!' is a polite thank-you for a present; ta is British informal for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Irish boy left in underground coming up cock-a-hoop

indicators.note: coming up says the letters read upwards, backwards in this down entry
in says the boy and left sit inside the underground's word

parts.note: the Tube is London's underground railway
Neil is an Irish boy's name

explanation.surface: An Irish boy left in the underground is delighted to come up to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebullient means bubbling over with high spirits, as is someone cock-a-hoop.

clue.text: Dead to bury after time moves on

indicators.note: moves on says the time letter shifts further along within the word for bury

parts.note: to inter is to bury

explanation.surface: The dead are buried once time has passed.
explanation.walkthrough: In INTER the T moves on to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Inert means lifeless and motionless, so it can stand for dead.

clue.text: Tense passion and rage superficially seen here?

definitions.text: Tense passion and rage superficially seen here?

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
heat means passion or intensity

indicators.note: superficially picks only the outside letters of rage

explanation.surface: Tension, passion and rage are what drama shows.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a playhouse, where these emotions are acted out.
explanation.definitionFit: A playhouse is where staged drama full of passion and rage is watched.

clue.text: Transport's concerning after near crashes put in a flat spin

indicators.note: after says the word for concerning comes after the other pieces
crashes says the letters of near are smashed into a new order
in a flat spin means in a panic, so the letters of put are jumbled

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: A transport vehicle nearly crashes and the passengers are thrown into a panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transport' looks like vehicles but means carry away with delight; 'crashes' and 'in a flat spin' each scramble their own short word.
explanation.definitionFit: To transport someone is to carry them away with delight, as to enrapture does.

clue.text: Go off place with scripture study firmly on the periphery

parts.note: to put is to place
RE is religious education, a British school subject

indicators.note: on the periphery picks only the outside letters of firmly

explanation.surface: Leave a place of scripture study firmly on the outskirts.
explanation.definitionFit: To go off is to rot, as food does, which is to decay.

clue.text: Admit crime and prisoner fine's reduced, initially expunged

parts.note: con is slang for a convict, a prisoner
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: initially expunged says the first letter of the word for reduced is struck out

parts.note: reduced means made less

explanation.surface: A prisoner admits the crime and sees the fine cut and the record wiped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' is LESS; 'initially expunged' removes its L, leaving ESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To confess is to own up to wrongdoing, exactly admitting a crime.

clue.text: Mediterranean city Romeo finds relatively pleasant

parts.note: Nice is a city on the French Mediterranean coast
R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Romeo finds a Mediterranean city rather pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of a word for pleasant means more pleasant, so relatively so.

clue.text: Do put in dossier as 'pointless'

indicators.note: put in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a dossier is a file of papers
ut is the old name for the note do in the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An office worker asked to put something in a dossier marked 'pointless'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' is not a verb here: ut is the old name for the first note of the scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Futile describes effort that achieves nothing, a synonym for useless or without purpose.

clue.text: Wanting to have touring lecturer with a collection of plants

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the word for wanting surrounds the lecturer

parts.note: to be for something is to be in favour of, wanting it

explanation.surface: Someone wants a touring lecturer to bring a plant collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Flora are the plants of a region taken together, or a catalogue of them.

clue.text: The boss man who thinks he's it

definitions.meaning: a knob or round projection, as on a shield or belt
a man who fancies himself as sexually attractive

explanation.surface: The boss is a man who thinks he is everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is both a raised knob and slang for a virile, self-admiring man.

clue.text: Understood garden bird swallowing a caterpillar's head

indicators.note: swallowing says the bird's word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: the tit is a common garden bird

indicators.note: head picks out the opening letter of caterpillar

explanation.surface: A garden bird gulps down the head of a caterpillar.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means implied or understood without being said.

clue.text: Work in iron say, making a bolt for it

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: iron is an example of a chemical element
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone working with iron makes a bolt for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolt' suggests ironmongery; here making a bolt for it is running off.
explanation.definitionFit: An elopement is a secret running away to marry, a dash or flight.

clue.text: Electronic network returns for a dreary tune

indicators.note: returns says the letters read back from the end

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail
a grid is a network, as in the power grid

explanation.surface: An electronic network plays a dreary tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a slow mournful song, such as a lament for the dead.

clue.text: She gives support in her column and a lot of care — leading to a tidy bundle

definitions.text: She gives support in her column

indicators.note: leading to says the first piece comes before the second
a lot of, but not all, says the last letter of care is dropped
to bundle is to stuff things together carelessly, so the letters of a tidy are rearranged

explanation.surface: A columnist dispenses support and care, leading to a tidy sum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Column' suggests an agony aunt's newspaper column; the support is architectural.
explanation.definitionFit: A caryatid is a sculpted female figure used as a column to hold up a building.
